title: Valuing Disputed Charges by Allowed Ratio on Internal Appeals to Contracted Commercial Plans (Insurance Coverage & Claims)
content:
**Reimbursement analysis memo — Insurance Coverage & Claims.** On an internal appeal that Halverson Clinical Laboratories files with a contracted commercial plan, the disputed charges are valued by the internal appeal's valuation ratio before anything else is figured on them.

## Allowed ratio

An allowed ratio is the plan's payment plus the member responsibility assigned, divided by that payment plus the contractual adjustment plus that member responsibility.

- The **claim's own allowed ratio** takes these amounts over the claim's lines: the plan's payments on the claim, the contractual adjustments on the claim and the member responsibility assigned on the claim.
- The **coverage's twelve-month allowed ratio** takes them over every such line on the coverage within the last twelve months.

## Valuation ratio

The internal appeal's valuation ratio is the claim's own allowed ratio where the remittance paid at least one line of the claim; it is the coverage's twelve-month allowed ratio where no line of the claim was paid but the coverage carries a plan payment within the last twelve months; otherwise it is one. The internal appeal's valued charges are its disputed charges times its valuation ratio.

## Input, judgement, output

| What the claim history shows | Valuation ratio | Valued charges |
|---|---|---|
| At least one plan payment line on the claim | The claim's own allowed ratio | Disputed charges times that ratio |
| No payment line on the claim, at least one plan payment on the coverage within the last twelve months | The coverage's twelve-month allowed ratio | Disputed charges times that ratio |
| No payment line on the claim and none on the coverage within the last twelve months | One | Disputed charges at billed value |

## Hypothetical example

A claim carries a plan payment of 72.00 USD, a contractual adjustment of 100.00 USD and member responsibility of 28.00 USD, and disputed charges of 300.00 USD. The claim's own allowed ratio is 72.00 plus 28.00, that is 100.00, divided by 72.00 plus 100.00 plus 28.00, that is 200.00: a ratio of 0.5. The valued charges are 300.00 times 0.5, that is 150.00 USD. Had no line of that claim been paid, the coverage's twelve-month figures would have been used in the same way.
